glosses: An excessive amount of something.

examples.text: A surfeit of wheat is driving down the price.

With what could be a surfeit of candour, [Mike] Skinner has described DJing as more creative than playing his own songs, because, to paraphrase, of the "stress" and "creativity" of not knowing what he'll be doing in three minutes' time.

glosses: Overindulgence in either food or drink; overeating.

examples.text:
I feel too much thy blessing: make it [this excess]less,
For fear I surfeit!
Now comes the sick hour that his surfeit made.
And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares.

glosses: A sickness or condition caused by overindulgence.

examples.text: King Henry I is said to have died of a surfeit of lampreys.

glosses: Disgust caused by excess; satiety.

examples.text: Now for ſimilitudes in certain Printed diſcourſes, I thinke all Herberiſts, all ſtories of beaſts, foules, and fiſhes, are rifled vp, that they may come in multitudes to vvait vpon any of our conceits, which certainly is as abſurd a ſurfet to the eares as is poſsible.

glosses: A group of skunks.
To fill (something) to excess.

examples.text:

glosses: To feed (someone) to excess (on, upon or with something).

examples.text: She surfeited her children on sweets.

glosses: To make (someone) sick as a result of overconsumption.

examples.text: […] that proportion of meat surfetteth, and surchargeth the stomacks of some, which is not enough to satisfie the hunger of others,
[…] I imagine him poisoned by his wines, or surfeited by a favourite dish;

glosses: To supply (someone) with something to excess; to disgust (someone) through overabundance.

examples.text:

examples.text: […] his appetite for vulgar praise had not yet been surfeited;

glosses: To become sick from overindulgence (both literally and figuratively).

examples.text: […] they are as sick that surfeit with too much as they that starve with nothing.
